subject: Meteorology
title: Morning Glory Clouds
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Morning Glory Clouds.

hook.text: In northern Australia, a giant rolling cloud tube can stretch 1,000 km across the sky—it's called Morning Glory.

buildup.text: This rare roll cloud appears most often over the Gulf of Carpentaria, usually between September and November.

discovery.text: It forms from the collision of two sea breezes meeting overnight—creating a massive atmospheric solitary wave.

twist.text: Glider pilots ride the Morning Glory like a wave—gaining altitude on the updraft ahead of the rolling tube.

climax.text: It's one of Earth's most predictable rare weather events—pilots fly from around the world to surf it.

punchline.text: A wave in the sky—and people surf it.

quiz.question: Where does the Morning Glory cloud most commonly form?
